title: Monica's tears (Confessions 3)
hookLine: a mother prays for years for her son; a bishop tells her a son of such tears can't be lost

cards: Augustine wrote his Confessions talking to God, not to us. We're overhearing. And in the third book he remembers his mother, crying.
He's a young man, brilliant, restless, and he has joined a religious movement called the Manichees, whose teaching he later left behind.

His mother, Monica, is a Christian, and she weeps over him, he says, more than mothers weep over a child's dead body. He's writing this long afterward, and he sets her tears down in a book addressed to God.

teach.h: A DREAM OF A WOODEN RULER.
teach.b: Augustine tells two moments. First, a dream. Monica dreams she's standing on a wooden ruler, grieving, and a young man, bright and smiling, comes up and asks why she's sad.
She says she's mourning her son's ruin.

teach.h: WHERE YOU ARE, THERE HE IS.
teach.b: He tells her to look: where she is, there her son is too. She looks, and sees Augustine standing beside her on the same ruler.
When she tells him, Augustine tries to twist it: maybe it means she'll come round to where he is. She answers straight away: no. It didn't say where he is, you are.
It said where you are, he is. Augustine admits her quick answer moved him more than the dream did. Second, a bishop, whom Augustine doesn't name.
Monica begs him to talk with her son and argue him out of his errors. The bishop refuses. The young man is too pleased with his new ideas, he says.
Only pray for him. He'll find out by reading. The bishop even tells her he went down that same road as a boy, and found his own way out.
But Monica keeps pressing, and crying. Finally, a little annoyed, the bishop says the line Augustine wrote down.
Go your way: it cannot be that the son of these tears should be lost.

teach.h: IT CANNOT BE THAT HE SHOULD BE LOST.
teach.b: Augustine says she took it as if it had sounded from heaven. Notice what the bishop didn't do. He didn't argue with the son.
He sent the mother back to her prayers.

how: Catholics honor Monica as a saint and some ask her prayers for children who have drifted from the faith; her feast falls the day before her son Augustine's.

o: a holy spring said to have healed the sick
a mother's long prayers for her wandering son
a sad hymn sung at funerals in old Carthage

p: a wooden ruler, and her son beside her
maybe she'll come round to him

s: Monica took the dream to mean she would come round to her son's views
that was Augustine's spin. she said: where you are, he is.
the bishop refused to argue with Augustine
he told Monica to let him alone and only pray; he'd find his way by reading.
Augustine names the bishop as Ambrose
he doesn't name him here. we meet Ambrose in Augustine's story later.

games.q: you're the bishop. a mother in tears begs you to argue her son out of his errors. what do you do?
o: call the son in and win the debate.
refuse, and tell her to let him alone and only pray.
tell her to stop crying; it won't help.
games.why: he refused, and when she kept pressing he told her the son of these tears could not be lost. she took it as a word from heaven.

practice: Bring to mind one person who feels far from you right now, far in miles, or gone quiet, gone another direction. Don't argue with them in your head; just hold them, and say their name.
If you pray, place them before God the way Monica did; if you don't, keep them in mind, warmly, without fixing anything.

wordCard.voice: Monica's tears. A mother's prayers for her son Augustine, and a bishop's promise that the son of such tears could not be lost. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the son of these tears — the bishop's words to Monica in the Confessions.

carryVoice: Your line: the son of these tears. Sometimes love waits instead of arguing. Day seven hundred thirty-three.
